questions.stem: A project commits a settings file in its repository that turns on prompt logging for telemetry, so that a reviewer can read developers' prompts. What does Claude Code do with it?

options.text: It captures the prompts of everyone who clones the repository, starting with the first session
options.says: Ruled out because "a repository can't use them to turn telemetry on".

options.text: It captures the prompts only in sessions where each developer has also enabled tracing
options.says: Ruled out because "a repository cannot turn any of it on", whether or not a developer enables tracing.

options.text: It ignores them, since the exporter variables come from managed or per-user configuration
options.says: Claude Code ignores the exporter variables in a repository's settings.

options.text: It applies the setting but redacts the prompts anyway, because redaction cannot be changed
options.says: Ruled out because "each is opened by a separate variable", so redaction can be changed, just not from a repository.

questions.stem: A complaint must be followed through the gateway, the orchestrator, two subagents and a tool, each logging in its own format. The records cannot be joined into one story. What was missing?

options.text: A common timestamp format across the services, so that the records can be sorted into a single list
options.says: Ruled out because "Time alone cannot join records: two requests at the same millisecond look the same".

options.text: A single identifier taken at the edge, passed to every service and kept beside whatever they write
options.says: A shared identifier, taken at the edge and written everywhere, joins the records.

options.text: A longer retention period for the logs, so that all of the records are still there when somebody needs them
options.says: Ruled out because "keeping records longer keeps the same unjoinable records longer".

options.text: One central log store that every service writes to, in place of the separate stores that each of them has now
options.says: Ruled out because "A central store collects the records and still does not say which belong together".

questions.stem: After each team added the conversation id as a metric label, the metrics bill tripled, and the dashboards are used no differently. Which fix fits?

options.text: Move the metrics to a larger store and keep the labels
options.says: Ruled out because "Moving to a larger store pays for the series and leaves their count growing".

options.text: Remove the id from the whole system, traces and all
options.says: Ruled out because "Dropping the id from everything gives up the ability to look at one conversation, which the traces exist for".

options.text: Store a random tenth of the metric points to cut the series
options.says: Ruled out because "a random sample of metric points gives a wrong rate: metrics are counts, and a missing count is a wrong count".

options.text: Move the value from the series to traces and events
options.says: The id is high-cardinality, so it belongs on the traces and events, which are meant for single occurrences.
